We compare the resulting inspirals with established radiation-reaction approximations, including the weak-field treatment of Peters and Kerr-based prescriptions from the literature, and use these comparisons to assess the qualitative behavior and limitations of the implementation. The modular structure of EMRICode allows the radiation-reaction prescription to be replaced independently of the underlying geodesic evolution, providing a framework for incorporating more accurate flux models and additional physical effects. We present two simple examples of how interactions with accretion disks and partial tidal disruptions can drive the evolution of a stellar EMRI orbit. EMRICode therefore provides a flexible computational framework for studying the orbital dynamics of EMRIs and for exploring extensions beyond the idealized vacuum, point-particle approximation.

title: Diffusive Description of Superconducting Single-Photon Detectors Using Quantum Mechanics
summary: The methodology of non-Hermitian quantum mechanics is employed to parameterize the dynamics of coupled classical diffusion equations describing low- and high-energy quasiparticles in superconducting single-photon detectors in one to three spatial dimensions.

title: A Radiation-Hardened, Fault-Aware Quantized Neural Network That Self-Heals
summary: Deep learning (DL) models are increasingly being deployed into radiation-challenging environments in spacecraft, particle accelerators, and, soon, space-based data centers. Instantiated as a learned orchestration of numbers stored in persistent memory, models are susceptible to continual degradation as high-energy particles corrupt data. At inference time, new data passed through the network fundamentally break the off-line assumptions and guarantees of a static model determined during training. To preserve the quality and efficacy of the models, fault tolerance against bit flips is a clear objective. In this work we developed a runtime method for repairing the quantized weights of neural networks (NNs) after bit flips on commodity, commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware, without storing extra replicas. Our work extends the well-established Fault-Aware Training (FAT) paradigm by adding an alignment penalty to concentrate undamaged activations and weights into a low-rank subspace, and we then reconstruct flagged corrupted coordinates from the uncorrupted survivors. We call this method {\it Projection Healing} and apply it to six regression benchmarks on quantized NNs. Holding a FAT checkpoint fixed and toggling only the runtime heal gives a further ${\sim}23\%$ reduction in the native-unit excess integral. Across those datasets the method extends the operational scrub interval by a median of $2.04\times$ at a $+5\%$ RMSE degradation and $1.96\times$ at $+50\%$, compared with $1.62\times$ and $1.07\times$ for classical Single Error Correction, Double Error Detection (SECDED). This introduces a new path towards designing resilient data-driven models, complementing established hardware redundancy, ECC, and FAT-based techniques.

title: Realization of de Sitter spacetime in AdS/CFT
summary: We construct horizonless, everywhere-regular solitons containing a de~Sitter core inside an asymptotically anti--de~Sitter spacetime, using an ordinary action of Einstein gravity, a Maxwell field, and a charged scalar. The object is a gravitating gauged $Q$-ball whose false-vacuum interior acts as a positive effective cosmological constant, sourcing an inner de~Sitter region joined through a thin wall to a charged, asymptotically AdS exterior. Two general requirements are emphasized: the scalar must lie in a near-false-vacuum (slow-roll--like) regime, and the exterior is driven to the extremal Reissner--Nordström--AdS locus in the thin-wall limit, in which the wall approaches the common would-be horizon. Since the solution is static and spherically symmetric, it may correspond to a semiclassical charge-$Q$ state of the dual CFT, realizing de~Sitter space approximately within a holographic theory. We also discuss free fluctuations whose de~Sitter--core modes appear as parametrically low-lying excitations above the state, bulk reconstruction, and the near-extremal regime, where finite-${\mathcal N}$ effects are expected to cut off the formal classical throat and replace its independent free-field modes by an interacting near-throat sector.

title: Mapping AdS$_4$ quantum gravity via the Bethe Ansatz formula
summary: The topologically twisted index of 3d ADHM theory can be written as a sum over solutions to the Bethe Ansatz Equations (BAEs) of the XXZ-type model constructed from quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{g}\mathfrak{l}_1$. Via a novel numerical algorithm, we solve for all $p(N)$ physical solutions at $N\leq 21$, where $p(N)$ denotes the number of integer partitions of $N$. Surveying these solutions, we find that in addition to the known "1-cut" solution dual to dyonic black holes, where the gauge holonomies are distributed along a single curve in the complex plane, there are "dressed" 1-cut solutions dual to combined configurations of the black hole and M2-branes, $m$-cut solutions dual to $\mathbb{Z}_m$ orbifolds of the black hole, a discrete family of solutions interpolating between the 1-cut and 3-cut solutions, together with other exotic solutions, at each value of $N$. The free energy of the interpolating solutions cannot be matched with the on-shell action of any known bulk solution. The $1,2,3$-cut solutions and interpolating solutions all have a well-defined large $N$ limit, and their leading order distribution of gauge holonomies can be computed analytically. Whenever possible, we fit the contributions of the solutions to the index to all orders in the $1/N$ expansion with high-precision numerics, and extract the leading non-perturbative correction. With exceptions, these are matched with the results of equivariant localization in the bulk, and the action of wrapped M2-branes respectively.

title: The shape of nonlinearity in binary-black-hole dynamics
comment: Public catalog of waveforms provided in https://tousifislam.com/VishveshwaraCatalog/; Software is provided in https://github.com/tousifislam/gwModels
summary: Black-hole perturbation theory remains remarkably accurate beyond its formal small-mass-ratio regime, but what limits this accuracy remains unclear. We develop a modular time-domain Teukolsky framework that isolates finite-mass-ratio corrections to the orbital dynamics while keeping the radiation at first perturbative order. Comparisons with numerical relativity show that the dominant source of discrepancy changes across the waveform. For nonspinning binaries, the available second-order dissipative flux removes $87\%$ of the inspiral rate discrepancy, bringing it to within $\sim1\%$ of numerical relativity. For precessing binaries, we identify a $ν^2\sin^2ι$ dependence in the inspiral time rescaling that is not explained by the leading orbit-averaged post-Newtonian terms, suggesting finite-mass-ratio corrections to precessional dynamics. Near merger, the same dissipative correction removes only $1$--$2\%$ of the discrepancy. We show instead that the merger offset is quantitatively accounted for by the difference between the initial Kerr background used in the perturbative evolution and the remnant black hole, with $96\%$ of the leading predicted frequency shift arising from the change in spin rather than mass. We release $1571$ time-domain waveforms for $348$ binaries as the Vishveshwara Catalog.

title: Density Accelerated Relaxation in Active Passive Colloidal Networks with Competing Interactions
summary: We investigate quasi-2D active-passive colloidal mixtures with electric field-mediated non-identical interactions: unlike species attract and like species repel. Mapping the steady states across total area fraction and active particle area fraction identifies the regime of active percolated network formation among active fluid and clustered states. Within the percolated network regime, relaxation speeds up with increasing density, contrary to expectations for dense particulate gels. Particle-resolved dynamics and microstructure link this acceleration to activity-driven rearrangements enabled by asymmetric interactions.

title: Flavor decomposition of electromagnetic multipole moments in $[q_1q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquarks: Light-quark analogs of $T_{cs1}(2900)^0$ with $J^P = 1^+$
comment: 12 pages, 5 tables,1 figure. The version is accepted for publication in Physics Letters B
summary: We present a systematic study of the magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments of compact $[q_1 q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquark states with quantum numbers $J^P = 1^+$, in the diquark--antidiquark picture and within the light-cone QCD sum rule framework. By performing a flavor decomposition across all admissible $u/d$ configurations, we show that the charm-quark contribution to the electromagnetic moments vanishes algebraically at the operator level -- a structural feature of the specific spin organization adopted here, in which the heavy antiquark resides in a pseudoscalar antidiquark, distinct from the dynamical $1/m_c$ suppression operative in alternative compact constructions and in hadronic molecules. The magnetic moments follow a coherent light-flavor pattern -- positive for $uu$-, negative for $dd$-, and suppressed for mixed-flavor diquarks -- and the quadrupole moments are non-zero throughout, corresponding, in the customary geometrical interpretation, to intrinsically deformed charge distributions. We further identify the dimensionless multipole ratio $\mathcal{D}/μ$ as a structural observable, independent of the normalization of the interpolating current, which probes the relative geometry of the spin-current and charge distributions complementary to the absolute moments. Taken together, the algebraic decoupling of the charm contribution and the operator-level distinction it implies among different singly-heavy tetraquark architectures constitute methodological signatures that discriminate among the corresponding internal organizations and, to the extent that a physical candidate is dominated by one of them, among compact and molecular interpretations.

title: Classical and Stochastic Trans-Planckian Censorship
summary: The trans-Planckian censorship conjecture (TCC) limits inflation to a deadline of $N_{\rm TCC}=\ln(M_{\rm Pl}/H_{\rm end})$ e-folds. We formulate it in stochastic inflation as a bound at confidence $1-δ$ on the probability that a history outlasts the deadline, with three readings: one worldline, the region grown from one Hubble patch, and the reheated volume. Each reading becomes a closed-form condition, rigorous for a linear roll in leading-order stochastic inflation (for the region, in a branching model) and sharp at leading order in $N_{\rm TCC}$: a linear roll whose classical history lasts $N_{\rm cl}$ e-folds respects the TCC if $1-N_{\rm cl}/N_{\rm TCC}\geq\{2\mathcal{P}_ζ[w+\ln(1/δ)/N_{\rm TCC}]\}^{1/2}$, with $w=0$ for a worldline and $w=3$ for a region. On a linear slope without vacuum decay, the worldline and region readings are never weaker than the classical TCC, and on the CMB-normalized attractor all readings agree closely with it, so the bounds on the scale of inflation stand. A classical phase that ends in a flat quantum well, which the overdamped classical TCC excludes, is allowed with a margin of a few e-folds per worldline. Near the onset of eternal inflation, the readings differ. On a linear slope, a region must leave the fraction $\sqrt{6\mathcal{P}_ζ}$ of the deadline unused at leading order: eternal inflation is excluded for every classical history that uses a finite fraction of the deadline, as is a band of non-eternal slopes, and the slope bound becomes $|V'|>V^{3/2}/[\sqrt2\,π(1-N_{\rm cl}/N_{\rm TCC})]$. Per worldline, every slope is allowed, given a margin of a few standard deviations. A false vacuum must decay at about the eternal threshold $Γ=9H^4/(4π)$ or faster for a region or the volume, but only faster than $3H^4\ln(1/δ)/(4πN_{\rm TCC})$ per worldline. Whether the TCC forbids eternal inflation depends on the reading.

title: Exact spectral integrability of a finite-channel random Schrödinger operator: from fermionization of the Dyson--Riccati gas to Kontsevich integral
summary: We solve exactly, for arbitrary finite channel number $N$, the Riccati dynamics of a quasi-one-dimensional random matrix Schrödinger operator with Hermitian white-noise potential in the $β=2$ unitary symmetry class. The associated Dyson--Riccati eigenvalue gas admits an exact free-fermion representation at any sample length $L$, which in the limit $L\to \infty$ expresses the density of states and the total Lyapunov growth rate exactly through a single Airy Hankel $τ$-function providing multichannel generalization of $N=1$ Halperin--Thouless formulas. The $τ-$function further admits an outgoing-contour Kontsevich matrix Airy integral representation. Its saddle-point and double-scaling analyses give, in a unified way, the finite-channel density Lifshitz tail, and the large-$N$ spectral edge. In particular, for $N\gg 1$ the sharp $N=\infty$ edge is softened within an $N^{-4/5}$ spectral window, with its profile governed by the tritronquée solution of Painlevé I. We conjecture universality of this quasi-one-dimensional scaling edge profile for a broad class of $β=2$ random band matrices.

title: High-cadence GW astrometry in the $μ$Hz gap
summary: We forecast the sensitivity of a dedicated, fast-spinning astrometric survey to a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) in the microhertz gap between pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and LISA. Spinning the satellite faster samples each star more often, raising the Nyquist frequency and opening higher frequencies at no cost in noise: the shorter, noisier exposures are exactly compensated by their number, so the white-noise floor of each position stream is independent of cadence. High frequencies are where astrometry is most competitive, because the deflection measures the strain directly: its strain noise is white, whereas the equivalent noise of pulsar timing grows as $f^2$. With a cross-correlation estimator over $N$ reference stars and the astrometric overlap computed in the distant-source limit, we find that a Gaia-like satellite scanning the ecliptic poles, with $N\sim10^4$ bright stars over $10$~yr, falls short of the background measured by PTAs by a factor $\sim\!60$. A larger, $8$-m-class aperture, or a constellation of satellites covering the whole sky, reaches it, while extending the reach continuously across the $μ$Hz band.

title: Nanoscale chemical engineering of Ti3C2Tx MXene multilayers through in situ electron beam irradiation in a TEM
summary: Defect engineering in low-dimensional materials is a powerful approach to tailor their structure and chemistry at the atomic scale, with high relevance for tuning physical properties. Here, we apply this strategy to MXenes, one of the largest families of two-dimensional (2D) materials, and demonstrate the use of a highly focused scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) beam for the structural and chemical nanoengineering of titanium carbide (Ti3C2Tx) multilayers. By adjusting the beam energy, electron dose, and scanning parameters, Ti3C2Tx multilayers were irradiated at 80 and 300 keV and characterized in situ using annular dark-field imaging and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS). The irradiation induces gradual structural and chemical modifications, largely driven by the selective sputtering of atomic species and MXene layers. We identify irradiation conditions that selectively remove Cl or F surface terminations while largely preserving the Ti3C2 framework, whereas other conditions promote preferential carbon removal, in agreement with theoretical predictions. Most notably, electron irradiation drives the migration and accumulation of initially dilute nitrogen impurities within the irradiated regions, leading to the formation of nitrogen-rich titanium carbonitride (Ti3CyNzTx) nanodomains embedded in the Ti3C2Tx multilayers. These laterally patterned carbide/carbonitride architectures constitute in-plane MXene heterostructures with nanometer-scale spatial control. These results demonstrate that electron irradiation can be used to locally tailor MXene composition and create nanoscale architectures beyond those accessible through conventional chemical synthesis.

title: From Harmonic Oscillators to Multiplicity Distributions in Particle Production Processes
summary: We propose an oscillator framework of studying multi-particle production processes using the information theory approach. For a system of degenerate oscillators, we derive the negative binomial distribution (NBD) and its nonadditive generalization represented as gNBD. We observe that gNBD derived from nonadditive statistics describes data in higher multiplicity region, thereby providing an alternative for the multi-component distributions used in phenomenological studies. We also generalize our framework for non-degenerate oscillators and encounter a Lerch-type generalization of the Barnes zeta function that, to the best of our knowledge, has not been studied in the context of nonadditive statistics and multiplicity studies before.

title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
summary: We show that the Yamazaki-Hori solution to the Ernst equation can be represented in the Pfaffian form. We also discuss the consequences of this result for Nakamura's conjecture on the relation between the Ernst equation and the 2D Toda model.

title: Central Limit Theorem for continuous $N$-particle systems in fixed- and high-temperature: single level
summary: We characterize central limit theorems for polynomial linear statistics of continuous $N$-particle systems on $\mathbb R$, in both the fixed-temperature regime $θ=β/2>0$ and the high-temperature regime $Nθ\toγ>0$. In each regime, we give necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of the coefficients of the logarithmic Bessel generating function, together with an explicit combinatorial formula for the limiting covariance. At fixed temperature, this formula recovers the classical second-order free moment--cumulant relation, up to the factor $1/θ$; at high temperature, it yields new second-order free $γ$-cumulants and their covariance relations. The proof combines moment extraction through Dunkl operators with a topological expansion of the logarithmic multivariate Bessel function indexed by ribbon graphs on surfaces. This expansion gives a topological interpretation of the free-cumulants: only genus zero contributes at fixed temperature, whereas arbitrarily high genera contribute at high temperature. As applications, we prove that $β$-addition preserves the CLT in both regimes and determine its limiting covariance from the input free cumulants, and establish a suitably rescaled transition from the high-temperature covariance to its fixed-temperature counterpart as $γ\to\infty$.

title: Local obstructions to trapped-region escape in modified gravity
comment: 5 pages, 1 figure; accepted for publication in Physical Review Letters
summary: Energy conditions in modified gravity are commonly imposed on an ''effective'' stress tensor that mixes physical matter with additional gravitational degrees of freedom, obscuring which sector actually controls null focusing, horizon multiplicity, and the disappearance of trapped regions. We develop a geometry-first alternative in spherical symmetry. For a normalized pair of future-directed radial null vectors, twolongitudinal Ricci projections and one independent transverse Einstein projection obey exact area-weighted transport laws. These imply a trapping-persistence theorem: after a nondegenerate future-outer marginal sphere, a regular ingoing generator cannot exit the trapped region while the ingoing longitudinal and transverse convergence channels remain nonnegative. In metric $f(R)$ gravity, with $F\equiv df/dR>0$, we then construct an entropy-resolved hierarchy based on the local Wald-density variable $Fr^2$. In the longitudinal entropy-focusing law, the scalaron second derivative cancels exactly, leaving a nonpositive scalar-gradient square together with the physical matter projection; in the independent transverse entropy-transport law, all scalaron derivative terms cancel. Entropy trapping is consequently governed by the physical matter condition $T_{nn}\geq 0$ and an algebraic mixed threshold rather than by a fictitious effective fluid. The resulting hierarchy cleanly separates matter positivity, geometric focusing, marginal-surface recovery, and gravitational-entropy evolution, and identifies the precise local reversals required for regular inner horizons, throats, and trapped-to-antitrapped transitions.

title: Soft elasticity of soft shells
summary: Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. Differential geometry deems as equivalent all surfaces in one and the same Bonnet family, but continuum mechanics is interested more specifically in soft deformation modes and the shapes they traverse, as they may describe ways to ignite fluctuations of soft shells that ideally require no energy to be activated. We give a general criterion for the existence of soft modes and a method to construct them based on a cascade of path integrations. We apply both criterion and method to some exemplary cases.

title: Partial reconstruction of the decay $B_{s}^{0}\rightarrow φ(K^{+}K^{-})η' (π^{+}π^{-}η)$
summary:
The decay $B_s^0 \to φ(K^+K^-)η'(π^+π^-η)$ is of particular interest in flavour physics because in the Standard Model it proceeds predominantly through the quark transition $\bar{b} \to \bar{s}s\bar{s}$. However, the reconstruction of this decay is experimentally challenging due to the presence of the neutral $η$ particle, which significantly reduces the overall reconstruction efficiency.
  In this study, the feasibility of using the partial reconstruction technique to reconstruct the invariant mass of the $B_s^0$ meson without explicitly detecting the $η$ particle is investigated. Monte Carlo simulated events corresponding to an FCC-ee environment are used, and the effects of detector momentum and vertex resolutions on the reconstruction performance are examined.
  The results show that improved vertex resolution substantially improves the global reconstructed mass response and partial-reconstruction efficiency, while improvements in momentum resolution are manifested primarily through a narrowing of the fitted central DCB component. These findings suggest that future high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ colliders such as FCC-ee could effectively exploit the partial reconstruction technique to study rare decay modes containing undetected neutral particles.

title: Holographic Reconstruction from Broken Conformal Gauge Symmetry
summary: We investigate bulk--boundary structures in $\AdS_4/\CFT_3$ from the viewpoint of gravity as a broken phase of conformal gauge symmetry. A crucial distinction is made between the Euler and Pontryagin characteristic classes. The gauge-theoretic gravitational action contains an Euler sector, whose total-derivative representation gives a boundary form depending on both intrinsic and extrinsic geometry. This structure is different from the Pontryagin descent to the three-dimensional gravitational Chern--Simons functional, whose metric variation gives the Cotton tensor and underlies the mixed boundary conditions studied by de Haro. We perform a Fefferman--Graham expansion of the Euler boundary form in asymptotically $\AdS_4$ spacetime. The normalizable coefficient $g_{(3)ij}$ does not contribute linearly to the finite Euler boundary term: its contribution from the cubic extrinsic- curvature sector vanishes by $\mathrm{Tr}\,g_{(3)}=0$, while curvature-- extrinsic-curvature terms containing $g_{(3)}$ vanish at the conformal boundary. A direct Codazzi analysis additionally shows that the Cotton tensor appears in the asymptotic mixed curvature but its contribution through the tangential-connection boundary variation vanishes for standard Dirichlet data. This indicates two distinct types of bulk--boundary structure: a global/topological Euler relation and a local Pontryagin--Cotton relation. We distinguish this kinematic Cotton appearance from a finite Cotton boundary response and discuss the implications for holographic reconstruction.

title: Quantum Fluctuations and Wigner Dynamics of a Carbon Nanotube Oscillator Driven by an Atomic Force Microscope
summary: Suspended carbon nanotubes provide a useful platform for studying controlled nanomechanical motion in regimes where environmental fluctuations, memory effects, and quantum coherence can all influence the dynamics. We model the fundamental flexural mode of a carbon nanotube driven by an atomic force microscope as a harmonic quantum Brownian oscillator subject to a prescribed classical force and coupled linearly to a thermal environment. Starting from the generalized Langevin equation, we formulate the reduced dynamics directly in phase space, where the Wigner function evolves through a Gaussian propagator determined by dissipative linear transport, a deterministic force-induced displacement, and bath-induced fluctuations. For a Drude memory kernel, the retarded response is expressed through the three roots of a characteristic cubic equation. In the classical-noise limit, the three independent entries of the finite-time covariance matrix reduce to explicit finite sums over these response poles, eliminating numerical double-time covariance integration. We extend the construction to the full quantum fluctuation spectrum, obtaining a thermal frequency series representation that retains zero-point and low-temperature fluctuations. For an initial two-packet superposition, we examine interference attenuation and the integrated negative part of the Wigner function, which provides a phase space measure of nonclassicality. These results provide an explicit analytical framework for finite-memory quantum Brownian motion of bound oscillators and a tractable phase space description of driven carbon nanotube dynamics relevant to future quantum state preparation and quantum tomography experiments.

title: Using Ricci Flow in the Construction of Homogeneous Cosmological Models
summary: This study develops numerical methods for computing homogeneous and isotropic cosmological models on manifolds with non-trivial spatial topologies. The use of Ricci flow is introduced here to aid in the construction of globally homogeneous initial data on these manifolds. The initial data produced in this way are evolved by solving Einstein's equation numerically to construct homogeneous and isotropic cosmological models on three exemplar manifolds in this study: Seifert-Weber space, the lens space $L(5,2)$, and Sixth-Turn space.

title: Structure and Dynamics of Defects in Two-Dimensional Nematic Liquid Crystals
summary: Topological defects in nematic liquid crystals have recently received renewed interest due to their important role in non-equilibrium active materials and developing biological systems. While many studies have focused on simulating defect behaviors in these non-equilibrium situations, there has also been recent progress in our analytical understanding of defect morphology and behavior in a number of complicated regimes, such as intricate boundary conditions, anisotropic elasticity, or the presence of flows. Here, we review the analytical theory of disclination structure and dynamics in two-dimensional nematic liquid crystals, highlighting recent methods and results.

title: Probing the $τ$ anomalous magnetic and electric dipole moments in photon-induced $γγ\toτ^+τ^-$ production at the FCC-hh
summary: The sensitivity of the FCC-hh to the anomalous magnetic moment $a_τ$ and the electric dipole moment $d_τ$ of the $τ$ lepton is studied in photon-induced $γγ\toτ^+τ^-$ production with both $τ$ leptons decaying hadronically. Central exclusive (elastic) signal events, in which both protons remain intact, are generated with MadGraph5_aMC@NLO using a FeynRules UFO model of the anomalous $γττ$ vertex merged with the TauDecay model, so that the $τ$ decays and their spin correlations are included in the matrix element. Single- and double-dissociative production is estimated with SuperChic and added to the elastic signal with its own coupling dependence and with normalisation and shape uncertainties of 25%. Pythia 8 decays the unstable hadrons in the signal, decays the $τ$ leptons and simulates the parton shower and hadronisation in the backgrounds, and hadronises the dissociated protons. Signal and backgrounds are passed through the Delphes simulation of the FCC-hh detector. Hadronic $τ$ decays are reconstructed from particle-flow tracks and photons with an algorithm based on the hadrons-plus-strips approach, with an efficiency of 73.4% within the acceptance. Requiring no additional tracks from the $τ$ vertices retains part of the dissociative contribution and reduces the Drell-Yan and $γγ\to WW$ backgrounds to 0.9% of the SM yield. The couplings are constrained from the shape of the total transverse mass distribution. For a centre-of-mass energy of 84 TeV and 30 ab$^{-1}$, the expected 95% CL limits are $-3.38\times10^{-4} < a_τ< 3.36\times10^{-4}$ and $|d_τ| < 1.88\times10^{-18}\,e\,$cm, about an order of magnitude beyond the current bounds. Results are also given for FCC-hh scenarios between 72 and 120 TeV and for an optimistic detector parametrisation.

title: Learning the open string spectrum with neural networks
comment: 44 pages, 13 figures, 1 Wolfram notebook attached with a custom made neural network
summary: The tree-level open superstring has an integer mass-squared spectrum on linear Regge trajectories. To what extent is this fixed by consistency conditions: locality, analyticity, crossing, unitarity together with the requirement that $2\to2$ scattering minimize the entanglement it generates? Using the local two-channel crossing symmetric dispersion relation with one-parameter ambiguity ($λ$-CSDR) we set up a bootstrap treating both the mass-squared spectrum and the partial-wave coefficients as unknowns which lets the machine learning algorithm to learn the mass-squared spectrum and partial-wave coefficients simultaneously, going beyond earlier work in which the spectrum was fixed. Using the local three-channel crossing symmetric dispersion relation with one-parameter ambiguity we obtain, within the class of amplitudes with soft Regge behavior and infinite higher-spin tower, a bound on the leading Wilson coefficients that we compare with existing bounds and trace to spin-0 dominance. We locate the Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude in the allowed region of the Wilson coefficients space. For amplitudes with two-channel crossing symmetry we find that a Non-dual amplitude exhibits a Polchinski-Strassler type transition from Regge to power-law behavior.

title: Minimality and stability of the ball for the charge-qubit energy
comment: AI tools were used in this project. All mathematical arguments and proofs in the final manuscript were checked and written by the author
summary: We study the shape optimization problem introduced by Mazzoleni, Muratov, and Ruffini as a model for a superconducting charge qubit, in which the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of a set of prescribed volume competes with the Coulomb self-energy of the ground state. We prove that, for sufficiently small charge, the ball is the unique minimizer, and that the energy deficit of a volume-preserving and centered perturbation of the ball is comparable to the squared $H^{1/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, with constants independent of the charge. We also obtain the corresponding results for the quadratic Hartree--Ohta--Kawasaki model.

title: Thermal and optical signatures of a magnetic AdS black hole in dark matter and quintessence
summary: We study a static magnetic anti-de Sitter black hole surrounded by perfect-fluid dark matter and quintessence. We follow the geometry from the horizon to the observer. We first examine the horizons and curvature. We then calculate the Hawking temperature and sparsity, weak light bending, the photon sphere, the shadow, strong-deflection coefficients, relativistic images, and simple Event Horizon Telescope size intervals. Because the model has several parameters, we use a one-dimensional benchmark path labelled by $η$. The point $η= 0$ is Schwarzschild, while $η= 1$ is the selected full configuration. This path is only a clear way to present the combined changes; it is not a new coupling. We derive the main relations step by step and test the weak- and strong-field approximations with direct numerical geodesics. Along the path, the outer horizon, photon sphere, critical shadow scale, and relativistic Einstein rings move outward. A formal solar-limb comparison gives $η\lesssim 2.06 \times 10^{-5}$ if the same local environment is placed around the Sun, but this is a source-dependent analogue rather than a universal bound. With the central mass and distance values used here, the M87* diameter allows $0 \leq η\leq 1$, while the adopted Sgr A* interval gives $η\lesssim 0.665$. Longer derivations, error propagation, and numerical checks are collected in the appendices.

title: Intrinsic Curvature Controls Spontaneous Entanglement of Elastic Rods
summary: We report results from an experimental investigation on the role of intrinsic curvature in the spontaneous entanglement of elastic rods subjected to controlled tumbling. We examine two distinct entanglement mechanisms, knotting and locking, in a statistical ensemble of straight and helical rods with varying arc length and natural curvature. Our primary finding is that natural curvature exerts a dominant, non-monotonic influence on knotting, with a critical curvature that suppresses knot formation and significantly reduces the probability of knotting relative to equivalent straight rods. In contrast, locking is largely insensitive to curvature and scales primarily with rod length. These results, obtained for the macroscopic experimental system studied here, identify geometric parameters that govern distinct entanglement modes in tumbled elastic rods and may inform entanglement processes in microscopic filamentary systems such as DNA.

title: Pulse Shape Model for a Light Enhanced Phonon Detector
summary: COSINUS has tested prototype NaI-based cryogenic scintillating calorimeters with a composite design, in which the transition edge sensor (TES) is fabricated on a separate carrier crystal coupled to the NaI target. Measurements with the composite detectors showed deviations from the known pulse shape description for cryogenic calorimeters and did not reveal an identifiable nuclear recoil population during a neutron calibration. In this work we present a new pulse shape model which provides an explanation to these observations and that laid the foundation for the development of the final COSINUS phonon detector design named remote TES (remoTES). We demonstrate that the first COSINUS detector prototypes featured a phonon channel with signal enhancement by light absorption in the carrier, namely a light enhanced phonon detector. This design offers for the first time the chance to use a single channel phonon detector for particle discrimination. We present recent results using a novel pulse shape fitting method based on the Bayesian inference software package BAT.jl.

title: Thermodynamic Supercritical Scaling Law for the charged Gauss-Bonnet AdS Black Hole
summary: The phase structure of the charged Gauss-Bonnet AdS black holes varies with the spacetime dimension. Within an appropriate parameter range, only the six-dimensional case admits two physical critical points and it is an ideal model for investigating supercritical thermodynamics in black hole systems with multiple critical points. In this study, we investigate the supercritical thermodynamic properties of this model in the extended phase space and construct the supercritical phase diagrams associated with the two critical points. The thermodynamic supercritical scaling analysis for the supercritical crossover lines in the vicinity of both critical points is completed, demonstrating universality. The corresponding coefficients for the external field scaling and the order parameter scaling are obtained, and their physical significance is discussed.

title: From Hermite Chaos to an Attractive Log-Gas: Explicit High-Rank Limits of Iterated-Logarithm and Tail Constants
summary:
Let $Z$ be a standard Hermite process of order $m\ge2$ and Hurst index $H\in(1/2,1)$. For $d<H-1/2$, let $Y$ be the variance-normalized version of the weighted integral $\int_0^1 x^{-d}\,\mathrm dZ(x)$. Its right tail satisfies $
  \log\Pr\{Y>t\}\sim
  -\frac12\left(\frac{t}{Λ_m}\right)^{2/m}, t\to\infty, $ where the positive constant $Λ_m$ admits an infinite-dimensional variational representation. The same constant governs the sharp law of the iterated logarithm for weighted sums of nonlinear functions of long-memory Gaussian sequences. A general closed-form evaluation at finite order is not known.
  As $m\to\infty$ with $H$ and $d$ fixed, the normalized constants $\sqrt{m!}\,Λ_m$ decrease to an explicit positive function of $H$ and $d$, with relative error $O(m^{-1})$. This function also gives a lower bound for the normalized constant at every finite order. An exact Rényi variational representation at each order yields, in the high-rank limit, the entropy--energy variational problem of an attractive logarithmic gas. The limiting free energy is evaluated through the Selberg integral and the Barnes $G$ function.
  For $d\le0$, convergence remains uniform up to the memory boundary $H=1/2$. After division by the square-root boundary factor $\sqrt{2H-1}$, the high-rank and boundary limits commute. Their common value is explicit; for constant weights it equals $2^{3/2}π^3G(1/2)^8=2^{11/6}πe\,\mathsf A^{-12}$, where $\mathsf A$ is the Glaisher--Kinkelin constant. The quadratic and cubic coefficients of the fixed-order expansion of the normalized constant as $H\uparrow1$ converge, as $m\to\infty$, to those of the explicit limiting function. Global finite-order bounds and a concentrating-weight limit complement the main result.

title: Stability Analysis of Axion Dark Energy Model
comment: 15 pages, 3 figures. Accepted for Publication in General Relativity and Gravitation
summary: We investigate the stability of an axion dark energy model characterized by a periodic scalar-field potential motivated by pseudo Nambu Goldstone bosons. While such models are well suited to drive late-time cosmic acceleration and can exhibit rich dynamical features, including oscillatory behavior of the dark-energy equation-of-state parameter, their viability crucially depends on the existence of stable cosmological solutions. By reformulating the background evolution equations as an autonomous dynamical system, we identify the fixed points corresponding to radiation-dominated, matter-dominated, and dark energy dominated epochs. Using both analytical and numerical techniques, we analyze the stability properties of these fixed points within the observationally allowed region of parameter space. Our results show that the radiation- and matter-dominated phases emerge naturally as saddle points, ensuring a standard cosmological evolution, while the late-time dark energy dominated solution acts as a stable attractor. This guarantees the robustness of cosmic acceleration against variations in initial conditions. Overall, our study establishes the axion dark energy model as a dynamically consistent and observationally viable candidate for explaining the late-time accelerated expansion of the Universe.

title: Reaction-induced Localized Annealing for On-chip Materials Discovery
summary: On-chip thermal processing is a key technology for materials discovery across all disciplines of the natural sciences. Here, we present a microfabricated heat-delivery platform that enables reaction-induced localized on-chip annealing up to 1400°C. A buried reactive multilayer combined with a nanometric diffusion barrier provide ultra-fast heating and quenching rates on the order of 10$^6$°C s$^{-1}$ as illustrated by the generation of ultra-high aspect ratio microstructures during rapid-solidification and the stabilization of dopant-free tetragonal zirconia at room temperature. Rapid kinetics also enable the observation of transient states of capillary-driven hole collapse in melts. Our work expands localized high-temperature processing routes and offers a material-independent approach for rapid screening of multidimensional nanomaterials on and off-equilibrium.

title: Soft elasticity of soft shells
summary: Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. Differential geometry deems as equivalent all surfaces in one and the same Bonnet family, but continuum mechanics is interested more specifically in soft deformation modes and the shapes they traverse, as they may describe ways to ignite fluctuations of soft shells that ideally require no energy to be activated. We give a general criterion for the existence of soft modes and a method to construct them based on a cascade of path integrations. We apply both criterion and method to some exemplary cases.

title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
summary: We show that the Yamazaki-Hori solution to the Ernst equation can be represented in the Pfaffian form. We also discuss the consequences of this result for Nakamura's conjecture on the relation between the Ernst equation and the 2D Toda model.

title: Invariant pseudo-unitary matrix ensembles and local statistics and conductance fluctuations of the DMPK ensemble
summary: We consider the DMPK ensemble, which models quantum transport in a disordered wire, and describe its limiting local statistics as the number of particles tends to infinity. In the metallic regime, as well as at crossover I, we obtain sine statistics in the bulk, Bessel statistics at the hard edge and Airy statistics at the soft edge. In the insulating regime, we prove localization around certain explicit deterministic positions with Gaussian fluctuations. This confirms and quantifies the predicted universal and localized behavior in the physics literature. At crossover II, we obtain explicit limiting kernels in the bulk and at both edges, which interpolate between these regimes. The hard edge kernel involves Legendre functions and, to the best of our knowledge, is new, while the bulk and soft edge kernels agree with those derived for the squared singular values of critically scaled products of independent Ginibre matrices. To explain these similarities, we construct a class of invariant pseudo-unitary matrices that is closed under taking products and use it to interpret the DMPK ensemble as the joint density of the spectral variables of a product of such random matrices. More generally, the latter takes the form of a polynomial ensemble of derivative type involving a second order differential operator compatible with the Legendre functions. Finally, we obtain uniform asymptotic expansions of the mean and variance of the conductance and prove that the DMPK ensemble admits universal conductance fluctuations, i.e. the variance of the conductance tends to $1/15$ throughout the whole metallic regime. This again confirms the predictions in the physics literature.

title: Thin-Shell Wormholes in Born--Infeld-Type Magnetic Spacetimes
summary: We investigate the radial stability, thermodynamic balance, and bilateral disk images of symmetric thin-shell wormholes built from Born--Infeld-type magnetic exteriors. The exact lapse and junction conditions define a fixed-mass family in which magnetic self-energy ties the nonlinear scale to the charge. The shell has negative energy density, although an inner sampled region satisfies the tangential null and intrinsic strong energy conditions. Linear radial perturbations yield unstable calibrated barotropic samples and stable sectors for the generalized and modified cosmic Chaplygin laws on selected real branches. Analytic horizon and large-radius limits explain the stability transitions and show how the modified linear pressure term can replace outer stability with finite radial intervals. Minimally coupled Maxwell rays traverse transparent junctions between exteriors with a common arctangent emission profile, viewed by a static observer. The wormhole-black-hole intensity difference separates transmitted disk light from emission removed by throat excision. Compared with static emitters, circular and plunging motion reduce the face-on intensities in the studied cases; inclined motion generates strong azimuthal contrast. Increasing the subcritical charge contracts the critical circle and permits more disk crossings near it in the optical samples. Under a reversible first law, flux cancellation gives isentropic motion at positive temperature, with entropy dependence left to a constitutive completion. These results distinguish geometric, material, and kinematic effects on shell support and disk illumination.

title: Chiral magnetic excitations in the RMn6Sn6 kagome metals (R=Tb, Ho, Er, and Y)
summary: Recent inelastic neutron scattering (INS) investigations of the kagome metal TbMn6Sn6 reveal novel chiral magnetic excitations associated with the kagome layer. These excitations appear to have an itinerant character with a large energy scale (> 100 meV) and heavy damping; however, the origin of these excitations, which are not predicted by local moment linear spin-wave theory, is not understood. Here, we use INS to show that chiral excitations are also found in RMn6Sn6 compounds with R=Tb, Ho, Er, and Y having uniaxial, tilted, planar ferrimagnet, and planar double-spiral magnetic structures, respectively. Thus, the chiral excitations exist regardless of the magnetic structure. Additionally, R=Er and Y demonstrate that the chiral mode intensity is weaker in planar magnetic structures, suggesting that excitations are transverse to the local Mn moment direction. The chiral excitations appear only at L=odd positions in the Brilloun zone, and correspond to chiral spin exciations of the same handedness within each kagome layer, and pi out-of-phase between layers.

title: Possible Microscopic source of torsion
summary: Axial fermionic interactions connect vacuum condensation with torsionful back- grounds. We consider a quartic spin spin interaction whose mean field reduction yields a quadratic fermionic Hamiltonian. Its diagonalisation defines a particle and antiparticle condensate, while self consistency determines whether the vacuum devel- ops a non zero axial current. Cutoff, fluctuation and energy conditions delimit the validity of the approximation. When torsion couples to spin, this axial expectation value can provide a microscopic source for an axial torsion background. We then consider mixed Dirac fields on such a background. In the explicit neutrino analysis, metric curvature is neglected while torsion modifies the flavour Bogoliubov coeffi- cients, producing spin dependent oscillation frequencies, condensate densities and CP asymmetries.

title: Learning the open string spectrum with neural networks
comment: 44 pages, 13 figures, 1 Wolfram notebook attached with a custom made neural network
summary: The tree-level open superstring has an integer mass-squared spectrum on linear Regge trajectories. To what extent is this fixed by consistency conditions: locality, analyticity, crossing, unitarity together with the requirement that $2\to2$ scattering minimize the entanglement it generates? Using the local two-channel crossing symmetric dispersion relation with one-parameter ambiguity ($λ$-CSDR) we set up a bootstrap treating both the mass-squared spectrum and the partial-wave coefficients as unknowns which lets the machine learning algorithm to learn the mass-squared spectrum and partial-wave coefficients simultaneously, going beyond earlier work in which the spectrum was fixed. Using the local three-channel crossing symmetric dispersion relation with one-parameter ambiguity we obtain, within the class of amplitudes with soft Regge behavior and infinite higher-spin tower, a bound on the leading Wilson coefficients that we compare with existing bounds and trace to spin-0 dominance. We locate the Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude in the allowed region of the Wilson coefficients space. For amplitudes with two-channel crossing symmetry we find that a Non-dual amplitude exhibits a Polchinski-Strassler type transition from Regge to power-law behavior.

title: On the Stability of Tolman Oppenheimer Volkoff Fireholes
summary: We investigate the radial stability of singular Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff fireholes with a radiation equation of state. These configurations contain a naked, negative point-mass singularity surrounded by a positive-density fluid, whose mass profile develops a Schwarzschild-like plateau before approaching an extended, self-similar atmosphere. Using the Prüfer phase method to identify the fundamental radial mode, we consider two outer boundary conditions: vanishing Lagrangian pressure perturbation (open firehole) and vanishing radial displacement (boxed firehole). For both, the fundamental squared frequency changes from positive to negative as the outer boundary exceeds a critical radius $R_c$. We find that $R_c$ follows approximately the same scaling with the central mass parameter as the equilibrium firehole radius $R$. However, the stability thresholds differ significantly: $R_c^{\rm O}<R$ for the open firehole, whereas $R_c^{\rm B}\simeq R$ for the boxed one. The regular zero mode is the derivative of the equilibrium family with respect to the inner lapse normalization at fixed central mass. This gives the boxed threshold a turning-point interpretation and, together with a scaling symmetry of the TOV equations, implies $R_c^{\rm B}\to R$ in the limit of large central mass. Variational bounds show that the rigid wall is the most stabilizing separated, self-adjoint outer boundary condition and that the unbounded configuration is unstable. Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff fireholes are therefore radially unstable unless confined within approximately their firehole radius.

title: Steering of topological criticality in the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain via non-Hermitian substitutional impurities
summary: We investigate the topological phase in a one-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain in the presence of a finite concentration of non-Hermitian substitutional impurities. Our primary focus is the discovery of a deterministic mechanism to actively reconfigure the topological phase boundaries by introducing site-dependent, non-reciprocal intracell and intercell hopping amplitudes. Specifically, breaking the internal structural symmetry of the non-reciprocal impurity hoppings induces a targeted macroscopic displacement of the critical point. This mechanism allows for the controlled expansion or compression of the topological phase strictly via local defect asymmetry. We validate this boundary displacement through finite-size scaling analysis. The extracted correlation length critical exponents ($ν\approx 1.455$ and $ν\approx 1.397$ for symmetric and asymmetric configurations, respectively) confirm a disorder-induced departure from the pristine SSH universality class, with the exponent diverging at high defect densities. We also report an impurity-induced real-to-complex spectral transition geometrically characterized by the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect. Ultimately, our results establish how isolated non-Hermitian asymmetries cooperatively interact to deterministically shift macroscopic topological protection.

title: Surface defects on lens space and transfer matrices
summary: We study surface defects in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ theories of class $\mathcal{S}$ and $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories of class $\mathcal{S}_k$ placed on $L(r,1)\times S^1$. The lens space index depends on the fugacities $p$ and $q$, and the effect of the defects on it is captured by difference operators acting on the fugacities and holonomies of flavor symmetries. For theories of type $A_1$ we determine in closed form the difference operators for the basic defects, labeled by $p^r$, $q^r$ and $pq$, and show that for odd $r$ there exist additional elementary defects, whose operators shift the holonomy by one half modulo $r$. All the operators commute, and the elementary operators generate the others. For even $r$ the same holds once the holonomy is extended to a twisted sector. We show that the elementary operators are traces of $L$-operators whose entries generate a Sklyanin algebra, with nome $q^r$ and shift $pq$. The lens space enters only through the parameters of the algebra and through its representation, which is realized on a doubled holonomy label. The $p$- and $q$-type algebras form a lens space version of the elliptic modular double. For class $\mathcal{S}_k$ theories we propose, and test in several ways, that the defect operators are transfer matrices of inhomogeneous spin chains built from these $L$-operators. Throughout, we use the TQFT structure of the lens space index, which follows from S-duality, both to fix and to check the operators.

title: Improved rapid phase ordering for Ising dynamics on random regular graphs
summary:
We study Glauber dynamics for the Ising model on random $d$-regular graphs with $n$ vertices at low temperature, in the regime $β\geq C/d$ where $C,d$ are sufficiently large constants. In this regime, the full mixing time is exponential in $n$, because of the bottleneck between the two dominant phases: configurations with a majority of plus spins and configurations with a majority of minus spins. We show that, for sufficiently large $d$, if the dynamics is initialized with an excess of at least $ε_{C,d} n$ plus spins over minus spins, then it quasi-equilibrates in time $O(\log n)$ to the Gibbs measure conditioned on positive magnetization. In addition, the required bias $ε_{C,d}$ can be chosen so that $ε_{C,d}\to 0$ as $d,C\to\infty$.
  Previous bound of \cite{GSS25+} in the Ising and large-$d$ setting required $β\gtrsim (\log d)/d$. A key difficulty is that, even from the all-plus initialization, one must control the propagation of negative information in spacetime in a low-temperature model with strong local correlations. We address this by developing a new bootstrap approach to proving subcriticality of disagreement clusters under the grand coupling.

title: Topological ModMax--AdS Black Holes: Extremality, Charge Normalization, and Limits of WGC Diagnostics
summary: We study four-dimensional topological anti-de Sitter black holes sourced by ModMax electrodynamics and its sign-reversed counterpart. Distinguishing the field-strength amplitude from the conserved displacement flux fixes the charge normalization, potential, and first law. We classify the exact extremal roots for spherical, planar, and hyperbolic horizons; in particular, the hyperbolic ModMax branch has no upper-charge discriminant bound and contains a finite-charge zero-mass point. We also derive the unstable spherical null circular orbit and evaluate the local near-horizon AdS$_2$ Breitenlohner--Freedman index for an explicitly specified charged-scalar probe. These are classical diagnostics, not a WGC verdict: the model does not specify a charged-particle spectrum, an ultraviolet completion, or the global perturbation problem. The distance and de Sitter conjectures cannot be quantitatively tested with the fixed-coupling AdS data considered here.

title: Nanocrystalline cubic boron arsenide growth on GaAs(100) by gas source molecular beam epitaxy
summary: Cubic boron arsenide (c-BAs) is a promising ultrahigh thermal conductivity semiconductor, but its direct synthesis on lattice-mismatched substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the synthesis of nanocrystalline c-BAs thin films on GaAs(100) substrates using gas source molecular beam epitaxy. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals an optimal growth temperature window of 250-400 C to maintain near stoichiometry and suppress severe arsenic loss. Surface and structural characterizations via atomic force microscopy, reflection high-energy electron diffraction, and grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction demonstrate a Volmer-Weber 3D island growth mode and a preferential crystallographic alignment with the GaAs substrate. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy confirms a chemically sharp interface without gallium interdiffusion into the c-BAs layer. These findings establish an initial step for the integration of c-BAs into advanced thermal and optoelectronic platforms.

title: Finite Spectral Recurrences for Loop Integrals in de Sitter and Anti-de Sitter Space
summary: We introduce a method that does for loop integrals in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter space what integration-by-parts identities do in flat space. A local, coordinate-free propagator algebra common to both geometries yields exact finite-difference equations in spectral labels; with external points they become differential-difference equations, and at the AdS boundary recover known Witten-diagram relations. Acting line by line, they apply in principle to any diagram. We solve them for the two-loop watermelon, isolating its ultraviolet poles, and for one-loop two- and four-point functions.

title: 5D Runge-Lenz Vector from Symplectic Reduction of 8D Harmonic Oscillator
summary: We derive the Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem from the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator through symplectic reduction. By rewriting the moment maps of the harmonic oscillator in terms of five-dimensional gamma matrices and the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ generators associated with the symplectic reduction, we identify the moment map expected to yield the Runge-Lenz vector. We then perform the reduction with respect to the SU(2) symmetry, derive the five-dimensional Kepler Hamiltonian, and show explicitly that the identified moment map reduces to the Runge-Lenz vector.

title: Geometrically Induced Semiclassical Limit for Quasinormal Modes and Greybody Factors in Higher-Dimensional Near-Ultracold spacetimes
summary: In this work, we investigate the correspondence between quasinormal modes (QNMs) and greybody factors (GBFs) in higher-dimensional Reissner--Nordstöm--de Sitter black holes based on the massless scalar field. Our analysis focuses on the QNMs in the near-ultracold family where the inner, outer, and cosmological horizons are close together. Under the geometric limit condition, the leading-order Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin term of the QNM is dominant for fixed angular quantum numbers and dimensionality without imposing the eikonal limit. Particularly, the corresponding GBFs also retain the explicit form of both parameters. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the half-transmission frequency of the GBF and its derivative are related to null geodesics, in terms of aspects such as the angular frequency and Lyapunov exponent, with the use of both parameters. We provide their relationships in arbitrary dimensionality. Furthermore, the higher-order corrections to the QNMs are investigated at the Nariai limit and in the near-ultracold geometry with separated horizons.

title: Magnetic-Field-Induced Darkening of Bright Excitons in a MoWSe$_2$ Monolayer Alloy
summary: Magnetic fields are widely used to brighten spin-forbidden dark excitons, but the inverse effect on an optically bright exciton has remained largely unexplored. We demonstrate the complementary phenomenon of magnetic-field-induced darkening of a bright exciton in Mo$_{0.68}$W$_{0.32}$Se$_2$. At 4.2 K, an in-plane magnetic field up to 25 T activates a dark-exciton line 14.2$\pm$1.3 meV below the bright exciton while suppressing the bright-exciton emission by about 85\%. A bright-dark mixing model quantitatively captures the coupled energy and intensity evolution with an effective in-plane $g$ factor of $|g_{\parallel}|=5.2\pm0.2$. Alloying is crucial to the effect, as it brings the system close to the bright-dark crossover, where a small bright-dark splitting is combined with unusually strong in-plane magnetic coupling. This places the system in a regime where field-induced level repulsion raises the bright-like branch and strongly depletes its thermal population. These results identify a general route to magnetic control of exciton populations through engineering of the bright-dark hierarchy.

title: Causality violation in the holographic approach to N=4 SYM theory at finite 't Hooft coupling
summary: In the AdS/CFT correspondence, correlation functions of the energy-momentum tensor in N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory at large but finite 't Hooft coupling can be studied using higher-derivative corrections to supergravity. We show that the commonly used holographic prescription for correlation functions which is obtained by truncating the equations of motion at order $(α')^3$ implies that the thermal equilibrium state of N=4 SYM theory in the planar limit is dynamically unstable at arbitrarily large finite 't Hooft coupling. The instability is a reflection of the unphysical causality violation brought about by treating perturbatively-derived equations as if they were non-perturbative, analogous to the instability of AdS black branes in five-dimensional Gauss-Bonnet gravity. While other holographic prescriptions for treating the $O(α'^3)$ corrections to supergravity may alleviate the pathology introduced by the truncation, the validity regime of the results obtained by any prescription at $O(α'^3)$ must be limited to the strict perturbative treatment of the $O(α'^3)$ effects on N=4 SYM observables.

title: Strichartz Estimates and Scattering for the Massless Reduced Dirac-Fock Equation
summary: In this paper, we establish Strichartz estimates for the reduced Dirac-Fock equation for 3D massless spinors, linearized around non-localized equilibria. Our analysis covers both the random field and the density matrix frameworks. As an application, we deduce scattering for the corresponding nonlinear problem with a high-frequency cut-off.

title: Quantum Bianchi IX Anisotropies as Inflationary Relics in the Primordial Spectrum
summary: Starting from the WheelerDeWitt equation, we investigate whether quantum anisotropies can survive inflation as relics of the preinflationary geometry and leave an imprint on the primordial curvature spectrum. We perform a BornOppenheimer separation of the wave functional into slow gravitational and fast matter components, justified by the hierarchy between the Planck scale and the lower matter scale, associated here with the inflaton. The full wave functional is then treated through a semiclassical WKB expansion in M to the minus 1, where M is quadratic in the Planck mass. The gravitational sector consists of a de Sitter background supplemented by homogeneous quantum anisotropies in the smallanisotropy regime of the Bianchi IX potential, while matter is represented by a single scalar inflaton field. At order M in the expansion parameter, the WheelerDeWitt equation reproduces the vacuum HamiltonJacobi equation with a cosmological constant. At order M to 0, the internal freedom of the BornOppenheimer factorization separates quantum field theory on curved spacetime from the anisotropy dynamics, described by timedependent harmonic oscillators. At order M to the minus 1, we obtain the quantumgravitational correction to matter. The anisotropy wave function enters explicitly the corresponding operator, so the corrected dynamics retains information about the Bianchi IX quantum state. The curvature power spectrum consequently contains two distinguishable contributions: one independent of the anisotropy state and a genuinely anisotropic term. The latter survives through the quantum variance of the anisotropies, thereby identifying the mechanism through which the preinflationary quantum geometry can affect the primordial spectrum.

title: Charge-conserving creation and annihilation of topological phase singularities in atomically thin semiconductors
summary: Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides provide a promising material platform for optical phase manipulation, as rapid variations in their dielectric functions can give rise to topological phase singularities (PSs). However, PS evolution while preserving topological charge conservation has not yet been investigated in exciton enabled PS systems. Here, using atomically thin MoS2 films on sapphire as a model system, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate that the evolution of dielectric dispersion determines the creation, trajectory, merging, and annihilation of optical PSs under topological charge conservation. By varying the MoS2 film thickness, we experimentally realize this evolution through the gradual shrinking of the high energy n-k dispersion loop, which modifies its intersection with the zero reflection condition. Our results provide a general strategy for exploring and manipulating topological optical states.

title: Cosmological correlators from the Euclidean sphere
summary: We propose a new framework for computing late-time cosmological correlators in de Sitter spacetime by analytic continuation from the Euclidean sphere. In this framework, correlators of arbitrary massive scalar fields take the universal form of generalized Euler integrals. Using this representation, we reproduce the results obtained using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism for a range of tree-level and loop diagrams, providing nontrivial checks of the equivalence between the Euclidean and the in-in formalisms. We further show that a Landau analysis of the generalized Euler integrals determines the singularities of the corresponding correlators in momentum space. This framework provides a systematic approach to studying the analytic structure of cosmological correlators.

title: Free-field realizations of $\mathcal{N} = 1$ supersymmetric $\mathcal{W}$-algebras associated with Lie superalgebras $B (n - 1 , n)$ and $B (n , n)$
summary: We extend the recursive construction of free-field realizations proposed by Ide, Ito, and Miyazaki to the $\mathcal{N} = 1$ supersymmetric $\mathcal{W}$-algebras $\mathcal{SW} B (n - 1 , n)$ and $\mathcal{SW} B (n , n)$, associated with the Lie superalgebras $B (n - 1 , n)$ and $B (n , n)$, respectively. We obtain explicit free-field realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (0 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$, and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$. In particular, the realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$ and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$ are new. Using these realizations, we compute central charges, conformal weights, and eigenvalues of the generating currents on free-field highest-weight states, and construct the local integrals of motion $I_1$, $I_3$, and $I_5$.

title: Finite-range hair from a nonlocal matter sector: charged Yukawa black holes
summary: { We construct a new exact charged, static and spherically symmetric black-hole solution of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with an additional anisotropic matter sector, whose metric is the Reissner--Nordström geometry endowed with a Yukawa-type contribution. The Yukawa term is exponentially screened: it is visible in the strong-field region but carries no independent asymptotic charge. We obtain an analytic parametrization of the extremal curve, identify the condition for higher-order degenerate horizons, characterize the curvature singularity and establish the weak, null, dominant and strong energy conditions. We further study the horizon thermodynamics, including the conjugate variables associated with the amplitude and range of the Yukawa sector and the corresponding generalized Smarr relation. The photon sphere, shadow, ray-traced appearance and quasinormal ringdown are then analyzed, with quasinormal frequencies computed through the sixth-order WKB expansion and confirmed, overtones included, by an independent spectral method. {Confronting the model shadow with Event Horizon Telescope measurements of M87* and Sgr A* constrains the finite-range sector directly, favoring its strongly screened, near-Reissner--Nordström regime.} This provides a unified geometric and phenomenological characterization of finite-range charged black-hole hair in ordinary Einstein gravity. }

title: Rashba-controlled emergence and reversal of critical-field anisotropy in p-wave magnet--superconductor hybrids
comment: 14 pages, 10 figures. Submitted to Physical Review B on October 6, 2026
summary: We show that tuning Rashba spin-orbit coupling can change the in-plane field direction along which an $s$-wave superconductor is most susceptible to Zeeman depairing. We consider a two-dimensional $s$-wave superconductor subject to an odd-parity exchange field induced by a $p$-wave magnet. Without Rashba coupling, the out-of-plane exchange field enhances the in-plane critical field but leaves its angular response exactly isotropic, despite the anisotropic magnetic spin texture. Minimizing the Bogoliubov--de Gennes grand potential over uniform singlet pairing, we find that increasing Rashba coupling first generates and then reverses the principal-axis critical-field contrast, switching the minimum-critical-field direction by $90^{\circ}$. Equal principal-axis fields at the intervening compensation point coexist with residual angular modulation. We interpret the reversal through competing momentum-dependent depairing contributions from the magnetic and Rashba spin textures, while the on-site singlet pairing channel remains unchanged. Direction-dependent discontinuous collapses of the order parameter further shape the critical-field curves. These results identify a tunable directional paramagnetic response within the uniform-pairing sector. In heterostructures with sufficient electrostatic tunability of interfacial Rashba coupling, this reversal would enable gate control of the easy-depairing axis without reorienting the magnetic texture.

title: Towards differential expansion for generic representations
summary: We report the first results of phenomenological analysis, based on extended set of explicitly calculated colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials in \cite{knotebook}. They concern differential expansion (DE), which separates the dependencies on the knot ${\cal K}$ and the representation $R$. %of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials. DE is well understood for symmetric and rectangular representations, while for non-rectangular $R$ even the knot-independent basis $Z_R^X$ of DE is not known. We concentrate on two issues: the possible derivation of DE and on improved characteristic of its defect. We discuss how evolution families -- twist knots, double braids and 3-pretzels -- can be used to find DE by a peculiar triangular transformation of evolution coefficients. Once $Z^R_X$ are found for particular family, they are expected to stay basically the same for arbitrary knots -- modulo controllable reductions, characterized by the defect of DE, which puts knots into different universality classes. Contrary to original expectation, these classes appear labeled not by a single number $δ^{\cal K}$, but by a whole non-decreasing sequence $\{k_j\}$, which is squeezed between two staircases, ${\rm entier}\left(\frac{j-1}{δ+1}\right)\leq k_j\leq{\rm entier}\left(\frac{j-1}{{\rm deg}\,Δ}\right)$, where the upper bound involves Alexander polynomial $Δ(q^2)$ and follows from the continuation of the Melvin--Morton--Rozansky-Kashaev limit to $A=q^{-m}$ with $m>0$, when the limit gives a {\it positive} power of Alexander. The old assumption $δ+1={\rm deg}\,Δ$ is oversimplified and fails for 19 non-alternating knots with 11 and 12 crossings. Last, we list the differences of non-rectangularly colored HOMFLY for various mutant pairs to demonstrate their universality (knot-independence) and nice consistency with the spirit of DE.

title: Scattering theory for bulk and surface waves in an impedance half-space, I: radiation conditions and a Rellich-type theorem
comment: 84 pages. Part I of a two-part series
summary: We study the negative Laplacian on the half-space $\mathbb{R}^n_+$, $n \ge 3$, subject to a constant impedance (Robin) boundary condition with $α> 0$. The boundary then carries a bound transverse mode, and at each energy $E > 0$ the system propagates two channels with the distinct wavenumbers $\sqrt{E}$ and $\sqrt{E+α^2}$: bulk waves decaying like $|x|^{-(n-1)/2}$ and surface waves decaying like $|x'|^{-(n-2)/2}$. The two rates are not comparable pointwise. Each is critical for the Agmon-Hörmander space $\mathcal{B}^*$, however. This Part I treats the flat boundary, and its purpose is to develop, at that endpoint, the scattering theory of the two channels in full. We prove a limiting absorption principle $\mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}^*$, construct the generalized Fourier transform, derive an expansion of the resolvent at infinity in which the two channels appear in a single relation, characterize the solutions of $\mathcal{B}^*$ growth, and compute the scattering matrix. The radiation condition is imposed on the solution itself, with no decomposition into channels, and is shown to be equivalent to the vanishing of the incoming data. The main result is a Rellich-type theorem whose hypotheses are imposed only near infinity and which forces both channels to vanish simultaneously. The surface channel turns out to be rigid: its block of the scattering matrix is the identity and carries no information about $α$, so that on the band $-α^2 < E < 0$ the scattering matrix is trivial. The bulk block, by contrast, determines $α$.

title: Monopole stability of time-dependent, spherically symmetric backgrounds in Horndeski theory
summary: We study linear perturbations about an arbitrary time-dependent, spherically symmetric background in the most general Horndeski theory. The odd-parity sector of such perturbations, analyzed previously, contains no scalar field perturbation and, hence, leaves the related degree of freedom unconstrained. In this paper, we address this issue by analyzing even-parity monopole ($\ell = 0$) perturbations, which isolate this degree of freedom. We derive the quadratic master action for the only propagating physical mode associated with the scalar field and formulate stability criteria which ensure the absence of ghost and radial gradient instabilities for the high-energy modes. These conditions are necessary for the stability of the background and complement the odd-parity ones. We show that they reproduce the known results in the static and cosmological limits. We also demonstrate that, in the cubic subclass of Horndeski theory on a dynamical background, the monopole criteria impose no constraints beyond those previously obtained for modes with large multipoles ($\ell \gg 1$). As an illustration, we apply the derived stability conditions for the monopole mode to a non-minimally coupled scalar field theory and to a black hole model with linearly time-dependent scalar hair; in the latter case, the monopole conditions further restrict the parameter space allowed by odd-parity stability.

title: Magnetic-Field Effects on the Electronic States of the K$_4$ Lattice
summary: We investigate the electronic states of the K$_4$ lattice in a uniform magnetic field within a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model. The K$_4$ lattice is a \rev{noncentrosymmetric three-dimensional network with triple-Dirac cones at the $Γ$ and H points}. By fixing the Bloch momentum component parallel to the field, the Peierls-substituted tight-binding problem reduces to an effective two-dimensional problem and yields a Hofstadter spectrum \rev{whose self-similar subpatterns reflect the geometry of the lattice projected onto the plane perpendicular to the field}. A square-like substructure emerges on the flux scale $φ= 1/8$ for $\bm{B}\parallel[100]$, and honeycomb- and triangular-like substructures emerge on the finer scale $φ= 1/32$ for $\bm{B}\parallel[111]$\rev{. Here $φ$ is the flux through the elementary plaquette of the projected lattice, and these scales correspond to one flux quantum per projected unit cell. Owing to the screw axes of the chiral K$_4$ network, the field-parallel momentum acts as an additional flux, which, for commensurate values of this momentum, shifts the spectrum along the flux axis and brings the second triple-Dirac cone at the H point into the magnetic spectrum}. In the weak-field limit, we derive the Landau-level structure from a low-energy effective Hamiltonian around the $Γ$ point. The three-component nature of the triple-Dirac cone gives rise to a cubic secular equation, whose solutions describe how a pseudospin-flat branch coexists with two relativistic Landau ladders \rev{and a single chiral $n=0$ level dispersing linearly along the field, in agreement with the lattice calculation}.

title: Universal Structure of Horizon Formation in Generic Binary Black Hole Mergers
summary: We derive the local structure of the first common apparent horizon in a generic binary-black-hole merger. This event occurs in the fully nonlinear regime, outside the standard regimes of post-Newtonian inspiral theory and perturbations of a stationary black hole, yet it admits a universal description. Without assuming symmetry, we show that the stability operator of the marginally outer trapped surface must lose invertibility at formation. Outermost stability then implies that the vanishing eigenvalue is the principal one, with a strictly positive eigenfunction. Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction yields square-root branch separation with a shared linear drift. Together these terms give a tilted parabola through linear order in time. The common horizon lies on a smooth marginally outer trapped tube tangent to the formation slice, and nearby later slices intersect it in outer and inner branches whose separation scales as $(t-t_*)^{1/2}$. Horizon quantities with a nonzero first response along the zero mode inherit the square-root separation and a shared linear term. We test these predictions in three binary black hole simulations, including an eccentric, precessing, unequal-mass system. In all three, the worldtube geometry and quasilocal scalars follow the predicted scaling. With the next-order term included, free-exponent fits to the surface geometry and quasilocal functionals recover $1/2$ to within half a percent, and diagnostics agree on the formation time within $5\times10^{-5}M$. The correlation between horizon shear and gravitational-wave news suggests that common horizon formation could have a signature in a short segment of the merger waveform.

title: Stability and instability for particle dynamics in magnetic fields
